_meta.title: SensorFM — Sensor Foundation Model for Wearable Health (arxiv 2605.22759, Google Research + DeepMind, May 21 2026)
_meta.context: Narayanswamy + Xu et al (Google Research + DeepMind + Univ. Washington + Univ. Oregon + UIUC, May 21 2026). First large-scale wearable-health foundation model — pretrained on 1 TRILLION minutes of unlabeled multimodal sensor data (5 modalities) from 5,000,000 participants across 100+ countries / 50 US states / 20+ devices. 4 size variants (XXS 10^5 / XS 10^6 / S 10^7 / B 10^8 params). Evaluated on 35 discriminative health tasks across 6 categories (Cardiovascular 6, Metabolic 8, Mental Health 8, Sleep 3, Demographic 4, Lifestyle 6) across 3 prospective studies (Metabolic 1,655 people, Mental 5,953 people, Sleep 6,377 people). Also paired with Gemini LLM 'classroom' (5 student LLMs autonomously search prediction-head architectures over 20+ cycles, 30,000 experiments) and Personal Health Agent (Gemini-powered with SensorFM as tool, validated by 4 clinicians × 31 patient profiles × 93 responses × 5 rubrics = 1,860 ratings). 75-page paper, 30MB. SensorFM-B wins 33/35 tasks vs supervised feature-engineered baseline; XXS ranks last on 33/35 (clean scaling).
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION. All scores verbatim from paper Sections 2.1-2.4 + Figures 1-4. 4 SensorFM size variants registered as distinct models. Headline aggregate metrics ingested as new benchmark IDs; individual per-task ROC AUC / Pearson r values (Figure 4 bar chart) deferred to a future per-task ingest (35 tasks × 4 sizes × demo-or-not = ~280 cells, requires careful bar-chart extraction). Daily-metric retention under 60-min ablation cited as headline numbers (Section 2.3). Classroom LLM scaling final-cycle scores extracted from Figure 2d (approximate end-of-cycle 20 values).

models.name: SensorFM-B
models._note: Largest SensorFM variant — 100M params (10^8). Pretrained on 1T+ minutes wearable sensor data from 5M participants. Wins 33/35 downstream health tasks; outperforms supervised feature-engineered baseline on 34/35. Mean ΔAUC = +0.09 vs XXS on classification; mean Δr = +0.21 on regression.

models.name: SensorFM-S
models._note: 10M params (10^7). Learns most tightly clustered latent representations among the 4 sizes.

models.name: SensorFM-XXS
models._note: Smallest variant — 100K params (10^5). Ranks last on 33/35 tasks (clean scaling lower bound).

scores._note: SensorFM-B wins 33/35 downstream health tasks across the 4 model-size panel (XXS/XS/S/B). Section 2.1.
Outperforms supervised feature-engineered baseline on 34/35 discriminative tasks. Section 2.2.
74.8% improvement on random missingness imputation over best-performing baseline. Section 2.3.
83.7% improvement on sensor signal imputation — strongest lift across the 4 generative tasks.
Daily step count retained at 99.7% accuracy with 60 contiguous minutes ablated (vs baseline drop). Section 2.3.

scores._note: XXS ranks last on 33/35 tasks (wins 0 head-to-head in panel). Clean scaling validates joint data+capacity scaling law. Section 2.1.
